[7, 13] The hurricane prompted major producers, including Ineos, Formosa, LyondellBasell, Baystar, and Dow, to preemptively shut down or modify their operations. [2, 12] These shutdowns, coupled with widespread flooding and power outages from the storm, led to logistical disruptions and complicated recovery efforts. Forge PolyFab, established in 2020 and based in the Dallas-Fort Worth area, specializes in manufacturing high-quality fabricated products from high-density polyethylene (HDPE). The acquisition is a strategic expansion for Winsupply in the HDPE market, aiming to enhance its product offerings for customers in the Dallas-Fort Worth Metroplex. [1, 5] This oversupply is anticipated to be worsened by the startup of new plants in China during the fourth quarter. [2, 3] The specific products affected by the force majeure included Terluran-brand ABS, Novodur-brand high-heat ABS, and Luran S-brand ASA resins. [3] The company stated it was working with local authorities and other industries to find solutions to increase water availability but could not estimate when production would restart. [3] <5> In April 2024, AmeriTex Pipe and Products announced the commencement of construction for a new manufacturing facility in Conroe, Texas, dedicated to producing high-density polyethylene (HDPE) and polypropylene (PP) corrugated pipes. [1, 2, 8] PE prices remained flat for the last three months of 2023 before an increase in January 2024. [9] A 3 cents per pound price increase by LyondellBasell effective October 26, 2023, was for Isopropyl Alcohol, not polyethylene. [6] A proposed 3 cents per pound increase for polyethylene in November 2023 did not successfully take effect in the market. <7> On November 8, 2023, Amcor, a global packaging company, and NOVA Chemicals Corporation announced the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) for a multiyear collaboration focused on mechanically recycled polyethylene (rPE). Under the terms of the agreement, NOVA Chemicals will supply Amcor with its SYNDIGO™ rPE resin for use in flexible packaging films. This resin will be manufactured at NOVA Chemicals' new mechanical recycling facility in Connersville, Indiana, which is expected to commence operations as early as 2025 and produce over 100 million pounds of rPE annually by 2026. The collaboration supports both companies' sustainability goals, including Amcor's target to use 30% recycled material across its portfolio by 2030 and NOVA Chemicals' ambition for 30% of its total polyethylene sales to come from products with recycled content. <8> Bayport Polymers (Baystar), a joint venture between TotalEnergies and Borealis, announced the startup of its new 625,000 metric ton-per-year polyethylene (PE) unit in Bayport, Texas, on October 2, 2023. This startup was later than the initially expected first quarter of 2023. The new unit, known as Bay 3, is the first in North America to use Borealis' proprietary Borstar technology. The expansion more than doubles the site's production capacity to over one million tons per year, significantly increasing North American PE capacity. This new plant is part of a larger integrated petrochemicals venture that includes a one-million-ton-per-year ethane cracker in Port Arthur, Texas, which came online in 2022.

[9] Specific indicators highlighted a modest upward trend, with the Cass Truckload Linehaul Index for April 2025 showing a 0.9% year-over-year increase. [9] Further data from the first quarter of 2025 showed a 3.0% year-over-year increase in linehaul spot rates and a 1.4% rise in contract rates, confirming an inflationary phase. The report also noted that while Less-Than-Truckload (LTL) volumes were soft, rates were climbing. Consumer spending saw a decelerated increase of 1.8% during the quarter as households contended with persistent inflation and higher borrowing costs. <10> In May 2025, Low-Density Polyethylene (LDPE) export prices in the United States saw an increase, driven by a marginal recovery in demand, particularly from Latin American markets. [1] A temporary suspension of certain US-China tariffs until August 12 contributed to a cautiously optimistic market sentiment. [1, 7] However, significant headwinds persisted, including a continuous oversupply of US-origin materials and high inventories among downstream processors, which exerted downward pressure on market fundamentals. [1, 6] This bearish sentiment was reflected in the broader market, with the North American LDPE Price Index declining by 8% quarter-over-quarter in the second quarter of 2025. [4] Without a substantial rise in demand from major foreign markets, prices were expected to remain under pressure. [6]
